title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
content:
Meta has launched what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States. Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs.
The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open-weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday.
Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and built for complex coding tasks and agentic labor. It has also been designed to run locally on Apple’s computers. However, you will still need a lot of power to run the model locally, with a requirement of at least 1 terabyte of RAM, per Engadget. The model will run best via the Mac Studio that comes equipped with the M5 Ultra chip.
Still, if you can muster the memory, Muse Spark Open may prove a significant work horse for coding and other desktop tasks. Meta says that it paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and deployed it to various agentic workflows, including coding fixes for a Mastodon client that included “bug fixes, new features, [and] full build.”
The company says it also deployed it in the service of running DaVinci Resolve, the high-end video editing software, revealing that the model was capable of reviewing and cropping footage.
Open-weight models provide a number of distinct industry advantages that aren’t afforded by closed and proprietary models. Open-weight models can be significantly more cost-efficient and can also offer transparency and flexibility that closed source models don’t allow.
Meta is making the new model available now through a number of different API platforms.

report.summary: Meta launched Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight, natively multimodal model designed to run locally on high-end Macs for coding and agentic tasks.
report.background: Meta’s release arrives as open-weight models are challenging closed AI systems on cost, transparency, and flexibility. While proprietary models still lead in some benchmarks, open releases let developers inspect, fine-tune, and self-host models for privacy-sensitive or specialized work. Apple Silicon’s unified memory architecture has made local inference increasingly practical, but very large models remain constrained by RAM. Meta’s new model targets that gap, positioning a frontier-scale open-weight model for Macs and agentic coding. It also reflects growing competition among US labs to claim the most capable open model, and among hardware makers to support local AI. The 1TB RAM requirement shows local frontier AI is still mainly for high-end workstations, not everyday laptops.
key_points: Muse Spark Open has 816 billion parameters, a 1 million token context window, and native multimodality. Meta claims it outperforms other popular open-weight models based on its own evaluations, positioning it for complex coding and agentic labor rather than casual chat.

Meta designed the model to run locally on Apple computers, but it needs at least 1 terabyte of RAM. The best experience comes on a Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra chip, making local use a niche, high-cost option rather than something typical Mac owners can try.

Meta paired the model with Muse Code, its AI coding terminal, and tested it in agentic workflows. In one case it handled bug fixes, new features, and a full build for a Mastodon client; in another it reviewed and cropped footage in DaVinci Resolve.

The model is available now through multiple API platforms. As an open-weight release, it offers cost-efficiency, transparency, and customization advantages over closed models, though Meta’s performance claims have not necessarily been independently verified.

The launch highlights a split in local AI: frontier-scale open models are becoming possible on high-end desktops, but their memory demands remain extreme. Most developers and users will access Muse Spark Open through APIs or cloud services rather than local Macs.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Muse Spark Open intensifies competition in open-weight models and pressures closed providers on price, transparency, and on-device capability. It also validates Apple Silicon as a serious local-AI platform, even if only for elite configurations. Developers gain a powerful, customizable model for coding and agentic workflows, but the 1TB RAM barrier means most will use APIs or cloud hosting; smaller quantized models and Apple’s MLX stack may benefit indirectly. Regular users are unlikely to run it locally today, but they may soon see its capabilities through coding assistants, video tools, and privacy-focused apps. The bigger signal is that frontier AI is moving toward open weights and local execution—while hardware remains the bottleneck.
report.tools: Follow Meta’s Muse Spark Open weights and Muse Code terminal. For local inference on Apple Silicon, watch MLX, llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio, though full 816B local use is impractical for most. For serving or experimentation via API/cloud, consider vLLM, Hugging Face, and Meta’s API partners. DaVinci Resolve is a useful test case for agentic video editing.
